openings.text: The key had been taped under the bench for years.
The bakery on Maple Street only opened at midnight, and nobody knew who baked the bread.
Somebody had sewn a tiny door into the lining of the umbrella that was left on the last train.
Every morning at seven, a goat in a yellow raincoat waited at the bus stop.
Nora found a postcard of a lighthouse that, according to every map, had never existed.
The old radio in the attic only played one song, and the song was a little different every night.
Max opened the freezer and found a hand-drawn map hidden under the frozen peas.
A new blue door appeared in the school hallway on Monday, and nobody would say who painted it.
The suitcase at the lost property office had a note taped to it saying not to open it before lunch.
The town cat was elected mayor again, and this time it had a plan.
The ice cream truck rolled into the village in November, and it only sold one flavor.
Overnight, somebody had knitted a scarf for every lamp post along the river.
A paper boat floated past the window every Friday at exactly four o'clock.
The garden gnome was in a different spot every morning, and it always faced the house.
Kai's bicycle bell rang by itself whenever somebody was about to tell a secret.
The little cinema showed the same film every night, but the ending was never the same.
Grandma's soup recipe had one line crossed out so hard that the paper tore.
The ferry to the island left at dawn with one passenger and a very large cake.
The elevator in the old hotel had a button for a floor that was not on any plan.
Inside the snow globe, a tiny light had come on in one of the windows.
The librarian slid a dusty book across the desk and said it was fifty years overdue.
At the night market, a woman was selling jars of fog, and the jar marked Tuesday was almost sold out.
The mailbox at number 9 got a letter every day, even though the house had been empty for years.
The smallest dragon in the valley was afraid of birthday candles.
The treehouse had a new room that morning, with a round window that looked out over the sea.
The night bus never stopped where the sign said, and the driver always hummed.
The teapot on the shelf started whistling, even though the stove had been off all week.
Someone had slipped a compass and a very old sandwich into Lena's backpack.
The village festival had one rule this year, and it was that everyone wore a hat that belonged to someone else.
A bottle washed up on the beach with a pizza menu inside, from a restaurant that did not exist.
The snowman in the park was still there in July, and children had started bringing it small gifts.
The town clock struck thirteen, and every pigeon on the roof looked up at the same time.
A tall ladder leaned against the clouds one morning, with a note on the bottom step that said back soon.
The piano in the empty hall played a single note each night, a little higher every time.
The cafe on the corner made cocoa with a secret ingredient, and today it ran out.
A fox in a bright red scarf waited outside the bakery, and it seemed to know Sam by name.
The kite had been stuck in the old oak for decades, until a message slid down the string.
The tent looked small in the shop, but inside it was somehow the size of a ballroom.
When the power went out in the apartment block, one window stayed lit and someone inside was laughing.
The museum guard had a favorite painting, and tonight the dog in it was missing.
